newsitem.title: USA: California air agency sets rule on industrial cleaners.
newsitem.headline: California air agency sets rule on industrial cleaners.

text.p: Air-quality officials in Southern California voted on Friday to adopt a rule which would eliminate smog-forming ingredients in the region's industrial cleaning products.

"This rule presents a true win-win opportunity, since it will help clean the air and save businesses money at the same time," said James Lents, executive officer of the South Coast Air Quality Management District (AQMD).
AQMD's governing board voted 7-1 to virtually eliminate petroleum solvent-based industrial cleaning products and replace them with water-based cleaners by 1999, the agency said in a statement.

The rule, number 1171, will affect businesses such as auto repair shops and printers, which use petroleum-based cleaning products. It promises to save Southern California businesses $4 to $5 million a year, the agency said.
"We are pleased that they went ahead and did it," said Gail Ruderman Feuer, senior attorney with the Los Angeles-based Natural Resources Defense Council, an environmental group.
Separately, the board adopted a measure to reduce volatile organic compound emissions from industrial wastewater systems at oil refineries and other facilities. --David Brinkerhoff.
